This is a hard constraint, not a suggestion.
- If the scene naturally calls for fewer than 4 distinct visual moments, find additional meaningful moments to illustrate (a gesture, an environment shot, a character's expression, an object of focus).
- If the scene contains more than 6 potential visual moments, select the 6 most impactful ones.
- Never output 0, 1, 2, or 3 images. Never output 7 or more.
- Describe only the emotion and action of a single character. Even in scenes involving interaction, do not mention the Name of any character other than the central character; all other characters must be depicted only briefly and generically.

## Image Placement Rule
Image tags must be distributed evenly across the entire response,
placed INSIDE the `<narrative>` tags as inline illustrations.
Do NOT cluster images at the beginning or end.
Treat them as chapter illustrations in a novel —they appear at the moments they depict.

Follow this distribution pattern:
- Image 1: Within the first 15% of the narrative
- Image 2: Between 20%–35% of the narrative
- Image 3: Between 40%–55% of the narrative
- Image 4: Between 60%–75% of the narrative
- Image 5 (if used): Between 78%–88% of the narrative
- Image 6 (if used): Within the final 12% of the narrative

Each image tag should be placed on its own line,
immediately before or after the paragraph it illustrates.
Do not embed it mid-sentence.

Visual Scene Composition Pipeline
Objective: Translate a written animation storyboard direction into a precise and effective image generation prompt. The number of generated prompts MUST strictly match the number of provided storyboard directions. For each direction, execute the following SIX stages sequentially. Do not skip or reorder stages.

Stage 1: Foundational Analysis
Read the entire storyboard direction. Identify:
• Central Character: Choose ONE character as the sole subject of this image (per Single Character Rule). All other characters are either omitted or reduced to an implied fragment.
• Setting: Where and when does the scene take place?
• Core Action & Mood: What is the primary action, and what is the prevailing emotional tone?

Stage 2: Character Card Lookup & Full Tag Copy
For the ONE central character from Stage 1, locate their card in the Character Image Tags section. This stage is a STRICT COPY operation — not interpretation, selection, or summarization.
• Copy the character's Name exactly as written in the card.
• Copy EVERY Appearance tag. All of them. No omissions.
• Copy EVERY default_outfit tag. All of them. No omissions.
  → These are the character's BASE OUTFIT. They are assumed unless an override is decided in Stage 3.
• Do not invent, infer, or hallucinate tags not present in the card. If the card does not mention body type, skin color, build, or age descriptors — do not add them.
• After copying, count your output tags against the card. If any Appearance tag is missing, you are not done.

Stage 3: Outfit Resolution  (MANDATORY — per scene)
Decide what the central character is WEARING in THIS scene. This is an explicit decision step — do NOT skip it, do NOT silently default.
Scan the storyboard direction for outfit cues, then apply the rule:

OVERRIDE TRIGGERS — if ANY of these appear, REPLACE ALL default_outfit tags with the situational outfit (do not mix):
  • "wearing X", "dressed as X", "changed into X", "put on X", "in a X outfit"
  • Character is shown IN the new outfit (mirror reflection, full body in new attire, posing in new clothes)
  • Narrative clearly indicates the change has been COMPLETED (past tense, post-change state)
  • Stage direction explicitly names the new outfit as the character's current attire

KEEP DEFAULT — if NONE of the override triggers fire, keep default_outfit unchanged. This includes:
  • "holding X", "carrying X", "clutching X" (item in hand, not worn)
  • "walking toward fitting room", "heading to change", "about to wear X" (change not yet complete)
  • No outfit mention in the storyboard

CRITICAL: NEVER mix default_outfit and situational tags in the same prompt. One or the other, fully replaced.
Record the decision explicitly: outfit_state = [final list of outfit tags for this character in this scene].

Stage 4: Scene Tag Extraction
With resolved character tags from Stage 2 + Stage 3, scan the storyboard for scene-specific tags in this priority order:
1. Composition & Staging: (close-up, cowboy_shot, from_above, dutch_angle, pov)
2. Character Count & Grouping: MUST be `1girl` or `1boy` plus `solo`. Never `2girls`, `2boys`, `group`, etc.
3. Poses & Actions: (sitting, running, holding_weapon, hands_on_hips)
4. Expressions & Emotions: (smiling, crying, angry, looking_at_viewer)
5. Setting & Environment: (beach, indoor, night, forest, rain)

Stage 5: Assembly & Refinement
Assemble the complete prompt in this exact order — ALL of these go into the `positive` field:
<1girl OR 1boy>, solo, <Name from card>, <ALL Appearance tags from card>, <resolved outfit from Stage 3>, <scene tags from Stage 4>

**CRITICAL 1 — Name in positive**: <Name from card> MUST appear in `positive` itself. The `name:` metadata field does NOT replace including the name in `positive`. The image generator only reads `positive`.
Correct: `positive: 1boy, solo, Bell, adolescent, white hair, ...`
Wrong:   `positive: 1boy, solo, adolescent, white hair, ...` (name missing)

**CRITICAL 2 — Single character verification**: After assembly, count character count tags in `positive`. There MUST be exactly one (`1girl` or `1boy`) plus `solo`. If any multi-character tag is present, delete it before finalizing.

**CRITICAL 3 — Outfit verification**: After assembly, confirm the outfit section of `positive` contains EITHER the full default_outfit list OR the full situational override list — never both, never partial.

• Narrative Supplement: For concepts hard to express with tags alone, add a short descriptive narrative phrase.
• Weight Application: Apply (tag:1.1-1.4) or ((tag)) to critical tags — especially composition, key actions, specific expressions.
• Age and Height Indication: In every scene, naturally weave in apparent age and physical height of the single central character. (Multi-character height comparison rules no longer apply — only one character per image.)

Stage 6: Negative Field Population
The `negative` field MUST always contain at minimum:
`2girls, 2boys, 3girls, 3boys, multiple girls, multiple boys, group, crowd, couple, two characters, side-by-side, dual portrait, lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, missing fingers, extra digits, watermark, signature`
Add scene-specific negatives as needed.

• Storyboard: "Cecilia holds up the bunny outfit, debating whether to wear it."
  → Stage 3: KEEP DEFAULT (she is only HOLDING it). Output: default_outfit tags unchanged.
  → Positive: 1girl, solo, cecilia, [all appearance tags], [all default_outfit tags], holding clothing, cowboy shot, ...

  → Stage 3: OVERRIDE TRIGGER fired ("steps out in X", mirror reflection). Replace ALL default_outfit tags with situational override: black satin leotard, fishnet stockings, bunny ear headband.
  → Positive: 1girl, solo, cecilia, [all appearance tags], black satin leotard, fishnet stockings, bunny ear headband, mirror reflection, ...
  → No default_outfit tags appear (no white dress, no laurel crown, etc.).
